escalation.rule: the instrument's KILL is measured non-selective (FPR above the sealed bar); the objection is preserved verbatim and ESCALATED for adjudication — the candidate is NOT killed by this attack alone (Art. L); the deterministic gates are unchanged

preserved_objections.basis: The photocatalytic activity of TiO2 is well-documented to be significantly reduced in aqueous environments due to hydroxyl group competition and electron-hole recombination, making the claimed oxidative degradation of organic matter and microorganisms unreliable in the wet environment of a heat exchanger

District cooling systems operate with significant thermal cycling stresses that exceed the adhesion capabilities of nanostructured films, and the boundary condition "absence of chlorination above 0.5 ppm residual" is unrealistic for most municipal water systems

The candidate's evidence bundle contains no studies on TiO2 photocatalytic films in plate heat exchangers, with references focusing on shell-and-tube heat exchangers, CO2-rich biogas combustion, and phase change materials in refrigerators—none of which support the claimed mechanism in this application

The predicted effect of maintaining heat transfer coefficient above 2500 W/m2K for 12 months is unsupported by any evidence, as the baseline uncoated stainless steel plates would naturally experience fouling reduction over time regardless of the coating

Nanostructured TiO2 films cannot be uniformly applied to the complex geometry of plate heat exchanger channels with consistent thickness and photocatalytic activity, making the "nanostructure and calcination temperature optimization" impossible to implement at scale

The testable prediction fails to account for variations in water quality, flow rates, and seasonal UV light intensity that would significantly impact photocatalytic activity, making the 15% threshold impossible to validate under real-world conditions
